title: What If the Sky Rained Candy?
habit: A candy storm makes everyday city life briefly magical and very sticky.
premise: A playful, scientifically grounded anime-style thought experiment about a candy storm over a city.

shots.what: A curious anime girl looks up as jewel-bright candies begin falling above a warmly lit city street.

narration.text: What if candy fell from the sky? It would look magical at first.

shots.what: Gummies bounce on curved rooftops and awnings while the girl opens a transparent umbrella and laughs.

narration.text: Gummies bounce on roofs. Jelly beans tumble as people rush out to catch them.

shots.what: A dreamy cutaway reveals a real cloud made from droplets and ice crystals while candy sparkles are marked as imagination.

narration.text: Real clouds are tiny water drops or ice. Candy takes magic.

shots.what: Close-up candies tumble through ribbons of air as size, shape and drag change their speed and path.

narration.text: Gravity pulls candy down. Size, shape, and air drag change its speed.

shots.what: Hard sweets tap harmlessly against a padded umbrella while soft gummies squash and spring back beside the surprised girl.

narration.text: Hard sweets could sting; soft gummies splat. Impact depends on their size and speed.

shots.what: A candy shell dissolves in rain and sticky water flows along the curb toward a storm drain.

narration.text: Rain melts the sugary coating, washing sticky runoff into storm drains.

shots.what: In a clear stream, microbes use oxygen as they break down dissolved sugar while fish move through the water.

narration.text: In streams, microbes use dissolved oxygen to break down sugar. How much matters; dilution matters too.

shots.what: The storm clears over the glowing city; the girl holds up one gummy with a sheepish smile beside the final takeaway.

narration.text: Magical at first. Sticky for longer. Would you try it?
